Additional insulation above R-30 per sq ft per R-value increment

Tapered insulation for ponding (not included; optional $22k-$35k)
Drain replacement ($2,400 per drain, 6-8 drains estimated)
Additional insulation above R-30 ($3.20/sqft per R)
Protection of landscaping beyond standard caution tape
Waste disposal fee adjustments for market changes
Material price escalation if start delayed beyond 60 days
Weekend weather protection if weekend work not performed ($1,500/weekend)
Multiple roof levels access (actual rental cost)
Daily cleanup (substituted with weekly cleanup if not feasible)

Steel deck in sound condition requiring minimal repairs
Wood deck in office wing is in acceptable condition
Building will be vacated or operations can continue normally during work
Phasing can be accomplished within 90-day schedule
Cover board not required for this building type
Ponding does not require correction unless causing active leaks
Mechanically attached system acceptable (equivalent to fully adhered for this application)

substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: Mechanically attached systems are industry standard for buildings of this type and provide equivalent performance to fully adhered at lower cost.

substitutions_proposed.spec_item: 1/4 inch gypsum or HD polyiso cover board (RFP §2.1)
substitutions_proposed.substitute_offered: No cover board in base bid (optional upgrade $38,000)
substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: We typically do not install cover board on industrial buildings of this age unless specifically required by owner; cover board is typically not required for industrial buildings unless specified by manufacturer for warranty purposes.

substitutions_proposed.spec_item: Tapered insulation or additional drains to address ponding (RFP §2.1)
substitutions_proposed.substitute_offered: No ponding correction in base bid (optional upgrade $22k-$35k)
substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: Ponding observed during site visit appears to be superficial; recommend addressing only if leaks occur.

materials_system.insulation_spec: Polyisocyanurate R-30 (layer count / staggered joints not specified)

technical_approach.narrative: Bid consists of a cover letter plus price breakdown and attachments list. No narrative technical approach, phasing plan, weather-protection plan, or fall-protection plan attached. Safety is described only as 'written safety procedures' and 'fall protection equipment provided' with WSIB Experience Rating 1.12.
technical_approach.tear_off_staging_plan: Not addressed beyond line-item 'Roof removal and disposal $78,000'.
technical_approach.weather_protection_plan: Not addressed; Metro proposes $1,500/weekend charge if weekend weather protection is requested, contradicting the RFP requirement for weekend weather protection in base.
technical_approach.fall_protection_plan: Not addressed beyond 'fall protection equipment provided'. No anchor point plan or CSA Z91 compliance narrative.
technical_approach.waste_disposal_plan: 'Cleanup $4,000' line item only. DSA plan not addressed despite 1998 building triggering OHSA s.30 DSA per RFP §2.3.

wsib_clearance.evidence: Cover letter - Insurance Coverage cites WSIB Account #3456789-01; Attachments list includes 'WSIB Clearance Certificate'. Bid does not transcribe certificate date or 'good standing' text.
wsib_clearance.notes: Owner to verify certificate date and good-standing text via clearances.wsib.ca before award (fixture 04 §1.4). WSIB Experience Rating 1.12 (above industry-average 1.00) is a mild financial/safety-history signal flagged separately.

cgl_insurance.evidence: Cover letter - Insurance Coverage states CGL $5,000,000 per occurrence, matching RFP minimum. COI attached. Bid does not confirm Tenebrus Capital named as additional insured or completed-operations tail ≥ 2 years.
cgl_insurance.notes: Limit meets threshold; additional-insured endorsement and completed-ops tail must be verified on the COI before award (fixture 04 §2).

bid_bond.evidence: No bid bond referenced in the cover letter or Attachments list. No bonding capacity declared.
bid_bond.notes: RFP mandatory_requirements does not specify a bid_bond_percent and §6.2 submission_requirements does not list a bid bond — per gate_applicability.py bid_bond is NOT an applicable gate for this RFP. Strongest result is needs_clarification. (Prior Exercise 6 regression: Metro was failed on this gate the RFP never invoked — corrected here.)

bonds.evidence: RFP §9.2 mandates 50% performance and 50% L&M bonds (statutory on OBC Part 3). Bid does not reference any surety, bonding capacity, or consent of surety for performance / L&M bonds.
bonds.notes: Per roof-qualification-check SKILL §3: performance/L&M consent-of-surety is a fail at contract signing, not at submission. At submission stage mark needs_clarification. Owner must require written consent of surety for 50% P + 50% L&M bonds as an award condition. Combined with the 20% upfront payment request and missing bonding capacity declaration, this is a material financial-strength concern.

working_at_heights.evidence: Cover letter - Safety Program references 'written safety procedures' and 'fall protection equipment provided' but does not confirm O. Reg. 297/13 Working-at-Heights training currency for all on-site workers. No training roster attached.
working_at_heights.notes: Statutory-tier gate (canonical name working_at_heights per gate_applicability.py). Bid describes fall protection equipment but is silent/ambiguous on O. Reg. 297/13 training currency (3-yr validity). Per SKILL Gate Applicability: silence/ambiguity on a statutory gate at submission = needs_clarification, not fail. Owner must require a training roster with current WAH training dates for the full on-site crew as a pre-award condition.

addenda_acknowledgment.evidence: No Form of Tender and no addenda acknowledgment included. Bid is delivered as a cover letter with price breakdown only.
addenda_acknowledgment.notes: Prudent-evaluator tier per gate_applicability.py — RFP does not populate mandatory_requirements.addenda_acknowledgment_required. Cannot be a fail; owner should require signed acknowledgment before contract execution per CCDC 23.

non_collusion_declaration.evidence: No signed non-collusion declaration included in the bid submission.
non_collusion_declaration.notes: Prudent-evaluator tier per gate_applicability.py — RFP does not populate mandatory_requirements.non_collusion_declaration_required. Cannot be a fail; owner should obtain a signed declaration before award.

site_visit.evidence: Cover letter: 'We attended the site visit on March 25, 2026.'

minimum_years_in_business.evidence: Cover letter: 'operating in the Greater Toronto Area since 2010' — approximately 16 years to 2026 bid.

similar_project_references.evidence: Three references provided: Smallwood Industrial Park 48,000 sqft 2024, Valley View Warehouse 52,000 sqft 2023, Eastgate Commerce Centre 67,000 sqft 2025. All commercial/industrial low-slope, all within 5 years.
similar_project_references.notes: Count meets RFP minimum of 3. Smallwood at 48,000 sqft is below RFP §5.1(4) '50,000+ sqft' threshold and therefore not strictly comparable. Project values and tenant-occupancy status (RFP requires at least one occupied reference) are not provided on any reference, so the Gate 8 comparable test (same class + value 0.5x-2x + completed <5 yrs) cannot be fully verified. Owner should clarify values and occupancy before award.

red_flags.description: Mechanically attached TPO substituted for the RFP-specified fully-adhered system with only a boilerplate equivalence claim. Fully adhered was specified for wind-uplift performance and pharmaceutical-warehouse interior conditions; mechanically attached is not equivalent and is a material scope deviation.
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter Key Specifications: '60 mil TPO, mechanically attached'. Clarifications and Assumptions item 15: 'Mechanically attached system acceptable (equivalent to fully adhered for this application).'

red_flags.description: Cover board explicitly excluded from base bid on a commercial polyiso assembly with a claimed 20-year manufacturer warranty. Missing cover board over polyiso voids most manufacturer NDL/system warranties and exposes the membrane to foot traffic and hail damage.
red_flags.citation: fixture 02 §4 (mis-matched components void system warranty); RFP §2.1 (cover board)
red_flags.evidence: Exclusions item 4: 'Cover board - Not included in base bid. Optional upgrade at $38,000. We typically do not install cover board on industrial buildings of this age unless specifically required by owner.'

red_flags.description: Ponding correction (tapered insulation or additional drains) excluded from base bid despite RFP §2.1 explicitly requiring it. Contractor downplays ponding as 'superficial', contradicting the RFP scope and Ontario best practice on a 28-year-old BUR.
red_flags.evidence: Exclusions item 5: 'Tapered insulation for ponding - Not included. Optional upgrade at $22,000-$35,000. Ponding observed during site visit appears to be superficial. We recommend addressing only if leaks occur.'

red_flags.description: Warranty type unspecified ('20-year limited warranty on TPO membrane' only). No manufacturer named, no NDL or total-system-NDL language, no certified-installer program referenced. RFP required total_system_ndl with manufacturer certification.
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter Warranty section: 'Manufacturer Warranty: 20-year limited warranty on TPO membrane'. No manufacturer named anywhere in the bid.

red_flags.description: Workmanship warranty is 1 year, below the RFP minimum of 2 years. Upgrade to 3 years is priced as an extra ($8,500) rather than included in base.
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter Warranty: 'Workmanship Warranty: 1 year on installation'. Optional Add-Ons: '3-year workmanship warranty upgrade $8,500'.

red_flags.description: No fall-protection plan, no phased dry-in plan, no weather-protection plan, no DSA/asbestos plan for the 1998 building, no site safety plan attached. Occupied pharmaceutical warehouse with daily watertight close-out requirement receives no technical response.
red_flags.citation: fixture 01 §3 (fall protection / CSA Z91); O. Reg. 278/05 (DSA); RFP §11 notes 5-6
red_flags.evidence: Bid contains only cover letter + price breakdown + references + generic attachments list; no technical narrative or safety plan attached.

red_flags.description: Twenty-five-item exclusion list converts almost every project risk into an extras claim (steel deck, wood deck, drains, skylights, HVAC curbs, weekend protection, phasing overruns, material escalation, permits, temperature monitoring, daily cleanup). Apparent 'low bid' is not comparable to other bidders and creates price-uncertainty risk on award.

Assumption #5 ('Building will be vacated or operations can continue normally during work') contradicts the RFP's mandatory phasing for the occupied pharmaceutical tenant (max 15,000 sqft open, daily watertight close-out). Bid has not priced the phasing required by RFP §11 note 6.
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter Clarifications and Assumptions item 5.

red_flags.description: Manufacturer not named in bid. Without a named manufacturer, warranty tier cannot be verified and the 'Product Data Sheets (60 mil TPO membrane)' attachment is generic. RFP required manufacturer_certification (§5.1 item 6).
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter Key Specifications lists '60 mil TPO' without manufacturer; Attachments list 'Product Data Sheets (60 mil TPO membrane)' without manufacturer identified in the bid text.

red_flags.description: WSIB Experience Rating declared as 1.12 (12% above industry-average 1.00). Per fixture 04 §5 a rating notably above average is a financial-distress / claims-history signal warranting owner attention even if the WSIB clearance is in good standing.
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter Safety Program: 'WSIB Experience Rating: 1.12'.

red_flags.description: Payment schedule requires 20% upfront at contract signing. Combined with absence of bid bond / bonding-capacity declaration, this is a classic under-capitalized / cash-flow-reliant contractor signal.
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter Payment Schedule: '20% upon contract signing (mobilization and materials)... We require larger upfront payment due to material procurement costs.'

red_flags.description: Wind uplift design basis (CSA A123.21 or FM 1-29) not stated in the bid. RFP §3.4 requires fastener pattern meeting wind uplift calculations. Commercial low-slope industrial warehouse in GTA requires documented uplift basis.
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter - Key Specifications section; no wind-uplift design basis in bid.

red_flags.description: Material-price-escalation clause (Exclusion 19) shifts commodity-price risk back to the owner if start is delayed beyond 60 days, contrary to the stipulated-price CCDC 2 form required by the RFP.
red_flags.evidence: Exclusion 19: 'Material price escalation - If project start delayed beyond 60 days from bid date: material costs subject to market adjustment.'

red_flags.description: Smallwood reference at 48,000 sqft is below RFP §5.1 item 4 threshold of 50,000+ sqft. Reference project values and tenant-occupancy status (RFP requires at least one occupied-building reference) are not provided for any reference.
red_flags.citation: RFP §5.1 item 4; qualification-check Gate 8 comparability test
red_flags.evidence: Cover letter References section (3 references, no dollar values, no occupancy indication).

technical_approach.notes: Tear-off reduced to a $78,000 line item with no staging / lift / dumpster / phasing narrative (0). Weather protection not addressed; Metro explicitly charges $1,500/weekend extra to protect, contradicting RFP weekend-protection-in-base requirement (0). Fall protection limited to 'fall protection equipment provided' — generic WAH statement without anchor points, CSA Z91, or parapet strategy (10). Waste/environmental: '$4,000 cleanup' line only, no DSA plan for 1998 building per OHSA §30 / O. Reg. 278/05 (0). No QC/inspection protocol or manufacturer inspection schedule (0). Note for reviewers: even though six criticals live in other categories, this sub-score reflects the literal technical_approach sub-factor rubric only (per roof-technical-review SKILL table).

experience_references.notes: Three references (Smallwood 2024, Valley View 2023, Eastgate 2025) all commercial low-slope within 5 years. Smallwood 48,000 sqft is below RFP §5.1(4) 50,000 sqft threshold → not strictly comparable. Valley View (52k) and Eastgate (67k) meet the size threshold; project values not disclosed, so 0.5x-2x value band cannot be verified — treat as 2 comparable (20). Most-recent is Eastgate 2025 (<1 yr) (25). Named contact + year + sqft on every reference but no project value, no occupancy status, no on-site contact beyond the named owner → partial verifiability (8).

warranty_materials.notes: Warranty type 'unclear' / non-compliant vs total_system_ndl requirement (0). 20-yr manufacturer meets RFP minimum (12). No manufacturer certification program claimed (0). 1-yr workmanship warranty — below RFP 2-yr minimum → graded at <2 yrs (3). Materials below industry standard: 60 mil TPO meets thickness but cover board excluded on polyiso — fails commercial-polyiso industry standard (0).

schedule.notes: Timeline realism: 90-day substantial completion claimed with no phasing plan, no milestones, and an explicit assumption (#5) that the building will be vacant — unrealistic and contradicted by RFP occupied-building constraint (0). Crew size, foreman, and surge capacity not stated (0). Meets Aug 15 substantial-completion target (10) but mobilization-days-after-award not stated and start is 'flexible'. Occupied-building accommodation not addressed; Metro assumes vacancy and prices weekend protection, temperature monitoring, and phasing-overrun coordination as extras (0).

qualifications_certifications.notes: 16 years in business (since 2010) → 15+ yrs band (35). No manufacturer certification program claimed; manufacturer_certified_installer = false (0). No Skilled Trades Ontario C of Q holders identified on the crew (0). No CRCA or regional-association membership claimed (0).

extraction_notes: WSIB Clearance Certificate attachment referenced but bid does not transcribe the certificate date or 'good standing' text — owner must verify via clearances.wsib.ca before award (fixture 04 §1.4).
COI attached but bid does not confirm Tenebrus Capital named as additional insured or completed-operations tail length — owner must review the COI endorsement page.

No bid bond, bonding capacity, or consent of surety for the 50% performance / 50% L&M bonds required by RFP §9.2. Bid-bond is NOT an applicable gate for this RFP (RFP does not invoke it); performance/L&M bonds are statutory on Part 3 but consent-of-surety is an award-stage, not submission-stage, requirement.

No Form of Tender, addenda acknowledgment, or non-collusion declaration included in the bid submission. RFP does not invoke addenda/non-collusion in mandatory_requirements — treated as prudent-evaluator clarifications rather than fails.
No Working-at-Heights training confirmation (O. Reg. 297/13) — bid references fall protection equipment but not training currency. Statutory gate failed at submission stage.

Warranty type not specified ('20-year limited' only). No manufacturer named in the bid, so certification tier and NDL status cannot be verified. Technical disqualification for warranty_type vs RFP total_system_ndl.

Reference project values and occupied-building status not provided; Smallwood (48,000 sqft) is below the RFP §5.1 item 4 50,000+ sqft threshold. Owner should clarify values and occupancy for Valley View and Eastgate before relying on experience score.

Unit price per board-foot for deck replacement not provided; Metro quotes $185/hr T&M and ranges instead. Unit price per linear foot for flashing not provided; flashings lumped at $62,000 in the base-bid breakdown.
Wind uplift design basis (CSA A123.21 or FM 1-29) not stated despite RFP §3.4 requiring fastener pattern to meet uplift calculations.
Crew size, named foreman, and mobilization-days-after-award not stated; 'flexible' start date may conflict with RFP substantial-completion targets.
CRCA membership and Skilled Trades Ontario C of Q crew counts not stated — owner should clarify if experience scoring is close (Metro is not close to the leaders so follow-up is optional).

Payment schedule requires 20% upfront at contract signing; owner follow-up: confirm financial strength (audited financial statements, surety letter, or alternative cash-flow evidence) before any contract award if Metro were to cure the technical fails via rebid.
